<findings>
<finding task="3"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>Count characters, as the spec says. Use `1 <= len(compat.strip()) <= COMPATIBILITY_CAP` with no `.encode('utf-8')`, change the error text and test name to "1-500 characters", and fix the comment "caps compatibility at 500 UTF-8 bytes". If bytes is what the owner wants, add an amendment to Task 1 and get the owner's approval. Either way, stop calling the Global Constraints line "copied verbatim".</fix></finding>
<finding task="7"><quote>CLAUDE.md's Commands section gains the `--strict` invocation with one line on when to use it (preparing a claude.ai upload or a spec-only validator run)</quote><plan>**D7** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-18): Task 7 names `--strict` in the frontmatter lint's existing CLAUDE.md comment and adds no line. Applied in: Task 7.</plan><fix>D7 changes what R1.9 requires: no invocation line is added, only a comment. That makes it a spec-level decision, so it needs an amendment in Task 1. Add an "A12" replace block to R1.9, tagged `(owner, plan 53, 2026-10-18)`. Log D7 as "Applied in: Task 1 (spec amendment A12), Task 7", and raise Task 1 Step 2's expected `plan 53` count to match.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>**State test changes as +N deltas** against the suite, never absolute totals.</quote><plan>Each expected summary line below is what the replay printed on top of `d70e0b3`; on a later base the absolute counts may differ, the deltas may not.</plan><fix>Restate every expected pytest line as a delta from the base run, for example "+4 passed, and the 4 new tests fail at RED". This covers Tasks 3–12's `45 passed`, `1 failed, 45 passed` and similar lines, and Task 10 Step 6's "(22, 9, 27, 268, …)". For suites with no change, write "count unchanged from the pre-task run".</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>The two existing `build.py` headers are the template.</quote><plan>## Decisions</plan><fix>The header the skill requires has no `## Review Focus` section. Add one between Global Constraints and Decisions, with the five likeliest untested failure modes, and give each a test in the task where it would fail. Candidates: `compatibility` with multibyte text near the 500 cap; a skill invoking a sibling skill's script whose floor is higher than its own; a script run with `uv run` from inside an unrelated project; an `agents/openai.yaml` with no `policy` key; and a skill directory holding a stray `LICENSE.md`.</fix></finding>
<finding task="10"><quote>Each rule gets a RED test first.</quote><plan>def check_script_headers(skill_dir: Path, vendored: frozenset[str] = VENDORED_SCRIPTS) -> list[str]:
    '''Each runnable script carries a PEP 723 block with requires-python and a
    dependencies list that declares every required third-party import
    (portability R3.7), so `uv run <path>` builds the environment it needs.'''</plan><fix>The plan is a transcript of the code. Tasks 3–12 carry full function bodies that their signatures and tests already determine, and the plan runs well over five times the length of the spec. Replace each code body with its signature plus the constants the spec pins, such as `PEP723_RE`, the alias table and the error strings. Keep the tests and the exact-copy edits.</fix></finding>
</findings>
